title: An encouraging sign from El Salvador: an aligned system and technology in service of learning can accelerate changes in Education
gist: El Salvador's 2024 education modernization program — an aligned system of curriculum, materials, teacher coaching, assessment and AI-enabled platforms — produced PISA for Schools scores of 492 in reading versus a 346-to-385 national baseline after roughly a year in around 200 schools, and the country is scaling toward 5,000 public schools while raising education spending above 8% of GDP from 2027.

themes.theme: Speed of reform as the contrarian claim

insights.claim: The assumption that 'change in education takes time' is itself costly, because students lose days and years that can never be recovered, and El Salvador is offered as evidence that rapid change is possible.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Reframes reform timelines: slow-reform orthodoxy is treated as a policy failure rather than a constraint, raising the bar for what governments should be expected to deliver within a term.
insights.quote: There is an assumption that runs through education policy: “change in education takes time,”
insights.locator: There is an assumption that runs through education policy

insights.claim: Before the pandemic around 69% of children in El Salvador could not read and understand a simple text by age 10, with structural causes including persistent inequality, resource constraints, difficulty attracting teachers and violence that disrupted school functioning.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Establishes the depth of the starting hole, which is what makes the measured gains notable rather than cosmetic.
insights.locator: El Salvador faces deep learning gaps

insights.claim: The program was deliberately staged: a pilot in 10 schools, expansion to about 200 schools in mid-2025, nearly 1,000 a year later, and a path toward almost 5,000 public schools nationwide.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: A five-fold-per-year scaling cadence is the operational benchmark to watch for whether fidelity survives expansion.
insights.locator: El Salvador's education modernization was designed as a gradual process

themes.theme: What the PISA for Schools data show

insights.claim: In July 2026, 1,198 volunteer students from 171 of the 200 first-phase schools took PISA for Schools and scored 417 in mathematics versus a national average of 346, 462 versus 385 in science, and 492 versus 366 in reading.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Gaps of 60 to 126 points after roughly one year in-program are unusually large for an education intervention and set the magnitude to verify at national scale.
insights.locator: In July 2026, 1,198 volunteer students took PISA for Schools

insights.claim: The authors explicitly caveat that the participating students volunteered and are likely among the higher performers in their schools, and that the results are not representative of the program or the country, while arguing the difference is too large to ignore.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Selection bias is acknowledged rather than hidden, so treat the effect size as an upper bound pending representative measurement.
insights.quote: the difference is too large to ignore
insights.locator: What the data show

insights.claim: The reading score difference is qualitative, not just numerical: at the national average of 366 a student can interpret a short text literally, while at 492 a student can independently locate information in more complex texts, draw inferences and connect information across parts of a text.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Translates score points into capability levels — the right way to judge whether a measured gain has economic meaning.
insights.locator: What do these scores mean?

insights.claim: The OECD notes the program schools' results are similar to the averages of Sweden and Germany, and in all three subjects they outperformed El Salvador's highest socioeconomic quintile in PISA 2022 and matched private schools in Chile.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Public schools in vulnerable settings clearing the local elite-private benchmark is the headline claim that will attract replication attempts and scrutiny.
insights.locator: The OECD notes that these results are similar

insights.claim: Many education reforms fail because components advance fragmented — technology is handed out without pedagogical support, students are assessed but results never reach the classroom — whereas in the program's schools curriculum, materials, teacher support, school leadership, technology and assessment advance together.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Gives a testable screen for judging any education or public-sector technology program: check whether the complements ship together.
insights.quote: Technology is handed out, but teachers get no pedagogical support. Students are assessed, but the results never reach the classroom.
insights.locator: Reforms work when they operate as a system

insights.claim: The reform prioritizes a foundational-skills curriculum in mathematics and reading, with per-grade essential knowledge, lesson plans and classroom guides built on the science of learning, in-person and virtual coaching, and continuous formative and summative assessment feeding real-time monitoring dashboards that trigger support for students falling behind.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: This bundle is the replicable product specification other ministries and edtech vendors will be asked to match.
insights.locator: The reform seeks to strengthen foundational skills

insights.claim: Two elements beyond standard best practice explain El Salvador's results: management and implementation capabilities built to deliver with fidelity across hundreds of schools, and technology that allowed integration at greater speed.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Delivery capacity, not program design, is the scarce input — the usual failure point when pilots scale.
insights.locator: These are the elements generally found in successful systems

themes.theme: AI as cross-cutting enabler, not a product

insights.claim: Almost all the actions in the reform could be carried out without technology; the difference is that when technology and AI are used well those actions happen more quickly, systematically and effectively, letting the system learn and respond faster.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Positions AI as a speed and coherence multiplier on an existing system rather than a substitute for one — the discipline missing from most edtech deployments.
insights.locator: Technology and artificial intelligence at the service of learning

insights.claim: Artificial intelligence and technology are conceived as cross-cutting enablers rather than a standalone intervention, and the authors concede they do not know the best combination of human capability and technology for each task, which depends on context and changes with the system's stage of development.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: An explicit admission of unknown optimal human-AI task allocation — the central open question for AI deployment in any public service.
insights.quote: we do not know the best combination of human capabilities and technology for each task in the education process
insights.locator: A distinctive feature of the education modernization program

insights.claim: El Salvador is working out the optimal balance between small language models and large language models depending on the specific task — assessment, coaching, or classroom observation — and refining tools according to how teachers and schools actually use them.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Task-level SLM-versus-LLM routing in a national public program is a concrete signal for inference-cost and model-mix demand in emerging-market public sector AI.
insights.locator: It also involves finding the optimal balance between small language models

insights.claim: No combination of human capability and technology in the program seeks to replace teachers; technology is framed as expanding what a teacher can do so they can spend more time on work requiring judgment and experience.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: The political precondition for AI adoption in education systems — deployments framed as teacher substitution tend to be blocked.
insights.locator: What is clear is that none of these combinations

insights.claim: Digital learning platforms in the program tailor experiences to each student's level, monitor attendance, track progress, identify students needing support early, generate content, strengthen assessment, and produce real-time information on where gaps are opening.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: The functional checklist for what a national learning platform must do to justify its cost.
insights.locator: In a system that faced attendance challenges

themes.theme: National results, fiscal commitment and financing design

insights.claim: El Salvador is one of only 12 countries worldwide with gains in mathematics, reading and science between 2022 and 2025, and together with Costa Rica the only one in Latin America, at a time when scores fell across OECD and middle-income countries alike.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: A rare positive outlier in a globally deteriorating dataset, measured before the modernization could have had much effect.
insights.locator: El Salvador is one of only 12 countries in the world with gains

insights.claim: Enrollment in El Salvador has begun rising as the country became safer, bringing in students from more disadvantaged backgrounds who would normally drag national averages down — yet national scores did not fall.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Composition effects make the flat national score a stronger result than it looks on the headline number.
insights.locator: Enrollment in El Salvador has also begun to rise

insights.claim: The government announced in August 2026 that it would raise education spending to more than 8% of GDP beginning in 2027, a budget commitment the authors call almost unprecedented in the region.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: An 8%-of-GDP education line is a material fiscal allocation to track against El Salvador's broader budget and debt path, and a procurement pool for education suppliers.
insights.quote: increase education spending to more than 8% of GDP beginning in 2027
insights.locator: From pilot to system transformation

insights.claim: World Bank support for the scale-up uses a Program-for-Results instrument, so the country receives disbursements as results are achieved rather than to finance inputs such as technology, materials or training.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Results-based disbursement shifts implementation risk to the government and is a structure to watch as a template for donor financing of AI-enabled public services.
insights.locator: The financial instrument being used is a Program-for-Results

insights.claim: The broader claim is that a system starting from very low levels can improve rapidly if it is conceived as an integrated whole that expands coherently, with political commitment and urgency treated as an indispensable condition.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Political commitment is named as the binding constraint, so regime continuity is the key risk to this reform's trajectory.
insights.quote: When learning becomes the priority and reforms reach the classroom, change in education need not take as long as we assume.
insights.locator: The political commitment to this goal
